coverage.DAT-002: State/HTTP Artifact tests enforce immutable ID/media type/size/digest metadata, owner authorization, bounded streaming and digest verification. Disposable PostgreSQL/MinIO tests prove authorized input/readback and reject forged or cross-principal references before staging.
coverage.DAT-003: Kernel and public StateRuntime cursor tests prove ordered bounded events, opaque replay/resume and explicit Gap semantics. Disposable producer-loss and durable publisher tests prove finalizable at-least-once delivery without silent loss.
coverage.DAT-004: Disposable PostgreSQL/MinIO producer-loss integration records a durable producer gap and terminal failure, then replays the ordered public Event sequence. The PostgreSQL/Temporal publisher integration reclaims acknowledgement-loss and process-kill routes.
coverage.DAT-005: Fake-clock cursor compaction/Gap tests and public Event contracts give clients a recoverable current-inspection path. Event retention is independently assigned by the planner's data-class policy.
coverage.DAT-006: The state planner test proves a distinct mutation appends without changing prior audit facts and an exact operation replay adds or changes none; the lifecycle vocabulary test requires attempted/authorized/committed and terminal/reconciled phases where applicable. Disposable PostgreSQL migration integration rejects a duplicate `(operation_id, fact_kind)` audit insert, while the durable outage integration proves audit retention exceeds its export route.
coverage.DAT-007: The concrete HTTP audit-exporter and disposable PostgreSQL outage integration retain a claimed exact audit route after a sink failure, reclaim it after lease expiry, export the retained fact, and record publication. The protocol is explicitly at-least-once, not transactional fail-closed.
coverage.DAT-008: The planner assigns named independent retention classes; the architecture inventory test requires every runtime-state class in the lifecycle documentation. PostgreSQL/MinIO collection and tenant-erasure integrations prove exact reference deletion/reconciliation, while the documentation states the separate payload and sandbox lifecycle authorities.
coverage.DAT-011: The runtime-state planner owns ordered runtime event sequence/cursor state. Producer-loss replay and PostgreSQL-to-Temporal publisher integrations retain PostgreSQL as the public event/cursor authority and exercise gap/finalization recovery without treating workflow transport as a public cursor.
coverage.DAT-012: Sealed-plan persistence, durable Artifact/model/tool paths, and PostgreSQL/Temporal acknowledgement-loss and child-process-kill integrations prove explicit transaction or at-least-once/reconciled boundaries. No stronger exactly-once effect claim is made.

limitations: DAT-001 remains unpromoted: current expected-version/idempotent Conversation coverage is planner-only; a Conversation-specific persisted PostgreSQL replay/conflict test is still required.

DAT-009, DAT-010, and DAT-013 remain unpromoted. The current PostgreSQL/MinIO/Temporal harness is disposable and does not provide an authorized protected-environment role-grant, scheduled-retention, active-WAL, isolated-PITR, or current production-configuration report.
The disposable backup/restore check is not a protected production backup/PITR drill, and no production operations claim is made.
